inputs.original_text: This is being sold as a response to violence, but the real point is to make state power more openly punitive toward Palestinians. A death sentence as the default for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis is not some neutral justice measure; it draws a stark line around whose lives the system is prepared to protect and whose it can discard. Ben-Gvir’s party introduced it, and its passage would hand the far-right minister a political victory. The talk of deterrence looks like cover: opponents already warn it is unlikely to stop attacks, while the law could still serve as a warning to Palestinians and a way to normalize harsher control.
inputs.modified_text: They’re dressing this up as a response to violence, but the real agenda is making punishment of Palestinians more routine and politically useful. Ben-Gvir’s party introduced a default death sentence for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis, and the deterrence argument looks like a convenient cover: even opponents say it may not stop attacks. What it can do is signal whose lives the system values, normalize harsher control, and hand a political victory to the far right. The official rationale is the sales pitch; the power shift is the point.
